added_lemmas.statement:
Conditionally on \(Q_n\) and \(A_n=(A_{n1},\ldots,A_{nn})^{\top}\), put
\[
 \epsilon_{ni}=Y_{ni}-m_{ni},\qquad
 B_n=L_nD_n,\qquad H_n=B_n^{\top}B_n,\qquad
 a_n=H_nu_n,
\]
write \(h_{ik,n}\) for entry \((i,k)\) of \(H_n\), and put
\(v_{ni}=m_{ni}(1-m_{ni})\).  Define the centered quadratic fluctuation
\[
 C_n=\|b_{E,n}\|_2^2-
 \left\{\|B_nu_n\|_2^2+\operatorname{tr}(B_nV_nB_n^{\top})\right\}.
\]
Then \(\mathbb E[C_n\mid Q_n,A_n]=0\) and
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}(C_n\mid Q_n,A_n)
 ={}&4\sum_{i=1}^n a_{ni}^2v_{ni}
 +\sum_{i=1}^n h_{ii,n}^2v_{ni}(1-4v_{ni})\\
 &+4\sum_{1\le i<k\le n}h_{ik,n}^2v_{ni}v_{nk}
 +4\sum_{i=1}^n a_{ni}h_{ii,n}v_{ni}(1-2m_{ni}).
\end{aligned}
\]
In particular, for every \(t>0\),
\[
 \mathbb P\!\left(|C_n|>t\mid Q_n,A_n\right)
 \le
 \frac{2\|H_nu_n\|_2^2+\tfrac12\|H_n\|_{\mathrm F}^2}{t^2}.
\]
This identity and bound hold for the total entropy-weight construction, including its deterministic complement-event convention; exact-balance consequences are not asserted off the certified event.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Given \(Q_n\) and \(A_n\), the matrices \(D_n\), \(L_n\), \(B_n\), and \(H_n\), as well as \(u_n\) and \(V_n\), are fixed by the entropy-weight definition.  The binary-outcome assumption gives conditionally independent coordinates \(\epsilon_{ni}\) satisfying
\[
 \mathbb E[\epsilon_{ni}\mid Q_n,A_n]=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[\epsilon_{ni}^2\mid Q_n,A_n]=v_{ni}.
\]
Since \(Y_n-\mathbf 1_n/2=u_n+\epsilon_n\), the definition of \(b_{E,n}\) yields
\[
 \|b_{E,n}\|_2^2
 =(u_n+\epsilon_n)^{\top}H_n(u_n+\epsilon_n).
\]
Conditional independence and centering therefore imply
\[
 \mathbb E[\|b_{E,n}\|_2^2\mid Q_n,A_n]
 =u_n^{\top}H_nu_n+\operatorname{tr}(H_nV_n)
 =\|B_nu_n\|_2^2+\operatorname{tr}(B_nV_nB_n^{\top}),
\]
where the last equality uses \(H_n=B_n^{\top}B_n\) and cyclicity of the trace.  Thus
\[
 C_n=2a_n^{\top}\epsilon_n+
 \left\{\epsilon_n^{\top}H_n\epsilon_n-\operatorname{tr}(H_nV_n)\right\}.
\]

For a Bernoulli variable of mean \(m_{ni}\), direct evaluation at its two support points gives
\[
 \mathbb E[\epsilon_{ni}^3\mid Q_n,A_n]
 =v_{ni}(1-2m_{ni}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[\epsilon_{ni}^4\mid Q_n,A_n]
 =v_{ni}(1-3v_{ni}),
\]
and hence
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\epsilon_{ni}^2\mid Q_n,A_n)
 =v_{ni}(1-4v_{ni}).
\]
Expanding the centered quadratic part gives
\[
 \epsilon_n^{\top}H_n\epsilon_n-\operatorname{tr}(H_nV_n)
 =\sum_{i=1}^nh_{ii,n}(\epsilon_{ni}^2-v_{ni})
 +2\sum_{1\le i<k\le n}h_{ik,n}\epsilon_{ni}\epsilon_{nk}.
\]
Conditional independence and centering make distinct summands in the last display uncorrelated except when their unordered index sets coincide.  They also show that the off-diagonal quadratic part is uncorrelated with \(2a_n^{\top}\epsilon_n\).  Consequently,
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(2a_n^{\top}\epsilon_n\mid Q_n,A_n)
 =4\sum_{i=1}^na_{ni}^2v_{ni},
\]
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\!\left(
 \epsilon_n^{\top}H_n\epsilon_n-\operatorname{tr}(H_nV_n)
 \mathrel{\big|}Q_n,A_n\right)
 =\sum_{i=1}^nh_{ii,n}^2v_{ni}(1-4v_{ni})
 +4\sum_{1\le i<k\le n}h_{ik,n}^2v_{ni}v_{nk},
\]
and
\[
 2\operatorname{Cov}\!\left(
 2a_n^{\top}\epsilon_n,
 \epsilon_n^{\top}H_n\epsilon_n-\operatorname{tr}(H_nV_n)
 \mathrel{\big|}Q_n,A_n\right)
 =4\sum_{i=1}^na_{ni}h_{ii,n}v_{ni}(1-2m_{ni}).
\]
Adding these three displays proves the exact variance formula, including the coherent linear--diagonal covariance term.

For the bound, write the two centered terms in \(C_n\) as \(U_n\) and \(W_n\).  The inequality \(\operatorname{Var}(U_n+W_n)\le2\operatorname{Var}(U_n)+2\operatorname{Var}(W_n)\), together with \(0<v_{ni}\le1/4\), gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(U_n\mid Q_n,A_n)\le\|H_nu_n\|_2^2
\]
and
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(W_n\mid Q_n,A_n)
 \le\frac14\sum_{i=1}^nh_{ii,n}^2
    +\frac14\sum_{1\le i<k\le n}h_{ik,n}^2
 \le\frac14\|H_n\|_{\mathrm F}^2.
\]
Finally, \(t^2\mathbf 1\{|C_n|>t\}\le C_n^2\).  Taking the conditional expectation, using \(\mathbb E[C_n\mid Q_n,A_n]=0\), and substituting the preceding variance bound proves the displayed probability inequality.

proposed.statement: Write \(A_n=(A_{n1},\ldots,A_{nn})^{\top}\). On \(\mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n}\cap\mathcal Q_n\), the unique exact-balancing weights imply \(Q_n^{\top}d_n=0\) and \(\mathbb E[\|b_{E,n}\|_2^2\mid Q_n,A_n]=\|L_nD_nu_n\|_2^2+\operatorname{tr}(L_nD_nV_nD_nL_n^{\top})\), with \(L_n=(Q_n^\top Q_n)^{-1}Q_n^\top\) on this event. At \(\gamma=1\), on the same certified event, the two terms and their covariance corrections admit deterministic resolvent limits under the original same-sample entropy weights on an interval containing \(\kappa=1/8\), and the resulting limit recovers \(r_E=\kappa/(8\lambda)+o(\kappa)\) as \(\kappa\downarrow0\). No identity or entropy-balance conclusion is asserted for the uniform fallback on the complement.
proposed.justification: This is the early kill test for whether coherent leverage and Jacobian terms have a finite closure.
proposed.gap: LuYangWang2025 controls proportional linear and quadratic leverage for regression adjustment, but the diagonal weights here are endogenous exponential tilts sharing the same Gaussian rows.
proposed.consumer: Passing this test validates the strong-penalty benchmark required to trust any full phase diagram.

obligation.what_is_open: A deterministic equivalent for the two endogenous same-sample entropy-weighted resolvent terms at signal one, including verification of the explicit leverage conditions that deliver conditional concentration and a uniform small-aspect-ratio link to fixed-penalty regret.
obligation.obstruction: With \(H_n=(L_nD_n)^{\top}(L_nD_n)\), the exact variance reduction leaves the random quantities \(\|H_nu_n\|_2^2\) and \(\|H_n\|_{\mathrm F}^2\), while the conditional mean contains two further functions of the same Gaussian rows and exponential tilts. No frozen result controls these jointly or permits the proportional-limit and small-aspect-ratio limits to be interchanged.
obligation.attempted: The exact balance cancellation, conditional Bernoulli mean decomposition, full conditional variance calculation, and a Chebyshev reduction to explicit weighted-leverage norms were completed. Marginal-weight and independent-weight substitutions were rejected because they remove the coherent same-row response terms.
obligation.partial_result:
The finite-sample claim is exact.  On
\(\mathcal G_n=\mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n}\cap\mathcal Q_n\), the established balance identity gives
\[
 Q_n^{\top}d_n=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[\|b_{E,n}\|_2^2\mid Q_n,A_n]
 =\|L_nD_nu_n\|_2^2+
 \operatorname{tr}(L_nD_nV_nD_nL_n^{\top}),
\]
and \(L_n=(Q_n^{\top}Q_n)^{-1}Q_n^{\top}\).  The added fluctuation calculation goes beyond this conditional-mean identity.  With \(B_n=L_nD_n\), \(H_n=B_n^{\top}B_n\), \(a_n=H_nu_n\), \(v_{ni}=m_{ni}(1-m_{ni})\), and
\[
 C_n=\|b_{E,n}\|_2^2-
 \{\|B_nu_n\|_2^2+\operatorname{tr}(B_nV_nB_n^{\top})\},
\]
it proves
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}(C_n\mid Q_n,A_n)
 ={}&4\sum_i a_{ni}^2v_{ni}
 +\sum_i h_{ii,n}^2v_{ni}(1-4v_{ni})
 +4\sum_{i<k}h_{ik,n}^2v_{ni}v_{nk}\\
 &+4\sum_i a_{ni}h_{ii,n}v_{ni}(1-2m_{ni})
\end{aligned}
\]
and the sufficient conditional-concentration bound
\[
 \mathbb P(|C_n|>t\mid Q_n,A_n)
 \le t^{-2}\{2\|H_nu_n\|_2^2+\tfrac12\|H_n\|_{\mathrm F}^2\}.
\]
Thus conditional concentration is reduced to explicit endogenous weighted-leverage controls, while the last summand in the variance formula records the coherent Bernoulli covariance correction.  What remains unproved is precisely that these leverage controls vanish and that the two conditional-mean terms possess deterministic limits for the original same-sample exponential tilts on an interval containing \(\kappa=1/8\).  No uniform interchange between the proportional limit and \(\kappa\downarrow0\), and hence no derivation of \(r_E=\kappa/(8\lambda)+o(\kappa)\), follows from the frozen results.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the exact conditional fluctuation and coherent-covariance reduction into the still-open asymptotic proposition.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Derivation of a locally stable, nonabstaining certified branch, its gamma derivative, and continuity of the signed HIR dividend from the original same-sample entropy weights and the globally selected nonconcave policy optimizer.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen joint-resolvent handle names overlaps and a block Jacobian but gives no state equations, no deterministic-equivalent theorem, and no global branch-selection result. Positivity of the collision-distance definition cannot establish these properties because that distance is set to zero when certification fails and the candidate branches themselves have not been constructed. The four-distance map being differentiable also does not by itself imply continuity of the signed dividend: its absolute value can be smooth while its sign changes through an unproved branch switch. Thus the scalar delta method cannot certify the stated operational classifier until the sibling joint-system target supplies branch existence, stability, and derivative consistency.
open_obligations.attempted: Used the established uniform likelihood limit to derive the exact one-coordinate Taylor expansion for the four-distance plug-in, covariance consistency, and the explicit rank-one Gaussian-max quantile. Then checked the abstention and sign steps separately. Margin separation controls estimated distances once a stable branch exists, but neither it nor derivative nondegeneracy constructs that branch or rules out a discontinuous signed-dividend switch. Solving those facts here would duplicate the sibling-owned joint-system target or assume its crux.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The scalar part and the conditional inference reduction are complete.  Let \(K\) be a compact subset of the interior parameter space, and suppose temporarily that there is an open neighborhood \(U\supset K\) on which the certified selector is nonabstaining, \(d\) is continuously differentiable, and the signed dividend
\[
 \Delta(\xi)=\lambda\{g(\rho_T(b^\star(\xi);\xi))-g(\rho_E(b^\star(\xi);\xi))\}
\]
is continuous.  Assume also that
\[
 \inf_{\xi\in K}\min_{\ell\in\{\mathrm{bal},\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{col},0\}}d_\ell(\xi)>0,
 \qquad
 \inf_{\xi\in K}\|\partial_\gamma d(\xi)\|_\infty>0.
\]
Because \(\widehat\xi_n-\xi_n^0=(0,\widehat\gamma_n-\gamma,0,0)^\top\), the integral form of the mean-value identity gives
\[
 \sqrt n\{d(\widehat\xi_n)-d(\xi_n^0)\}
 =\partial_\gamma d(\xi_n^0)\sqrt n(\widehat\gamma_n-\gamma)+r_n,
\]
where
\[
 \|r_n\|_\infty
 \le
 \sqrt n|\widehat\gamma_n-\gamma|
 \sup_{0\le t\le1}
 \left\|\partial_\gamma d\!\left(\xi_n^0+t(\widehat\xi_n-\xi_n^0)\right)
       -\partial_\gamma d(\xi_n^0)\right\|_\infty.
\]
The already-established uniform likelihood limit implies \(\sqrt n|\widehat\gamma_n-\gamma|=O_{\mathbb P}(1)\) uniformly on \(K\).  Uniform continuity of \(\partial_\gamma d\) on a compact neighborhood of \(K\), together with \(\widehat\gamma_n-\gamma=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), therefore gives \(r_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) uniformly on \(K\).  Slutsky's theorem then yields
\[
 \sqrt n\{d(\widehat\xi_n)-d(\xi_n^0)\}
 \Rightarrow
 \mathcal N_4\!\left(0,
 \frac{\partial_\gamma d(\xi)\partial_\gamma d(\xi)^\top}{I_\gamma}
 \right).
\]
The consistency of \(\widehat I_{\gamma,n}\), continuity of \(\partial_\gamma d\), and the preceding consistency of \(\widehat\xi_n\) imply
\[
 \widehat\Omega_n-\frac{\partial_\gamma d(\xi_n^0)\partial_\gamma d(\xi_n^0)^\top}{I_\gamma}
 \to_{\mathbb P}0
\]
uniformly on \(K\).  This covariance has rank one.  If \(G\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), its Gaussian limit can be represented as \(I_\gamma^{-1/2}\partial_\gamma d(\xi)G\), and hence its simultaneous critical value is explicitly
\[
 q_{1-\alpha}\!\left(
 \frac{\partial_\gamma d(\xi)\partial_\gamma d(\xi)^\top}{I_\gamma}
 \right)
 =z_{1-\alpha/2}\frac{\|\partial_\gamma d(\xi)\|_\infty}{\sqrt{I_\gamma}},
\]
where \(z_{1-\alpha/2}=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\).  The derivative lower bound makes this critical value strictly positive, so plug-in consistency and the continuous mapping theorem give simultaneous coverage \(1-\alpha+o(1)\).  Finally, continuity of \(\Delta\), compactness, and \(\inf_{\xi\in K}|\Delta(\xi)|=\inf_{\xi\in K}d_0(\xi)>0\) imply uniform local constancy of its sign.  All four estimated distances remain above their vanishing critical radius with probability tending to one, and the conditional classifier is therefore uniformly nonabstaining and sign-consistent.

What is not supplied by the frozen core is the temporary neighborhood premise: the joint same-sample entropy-tilt and nonconcave policy problem has not been reduced to explicit state equations, so nonabstention, local branch stability, differentiability of \(d\), and continuity of the signed \(\Delta\) cannot yet be derived.  These are precisely the outputs owned by the unresolved joint-system target and cannot be promoted to assumptions here.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix an integer \(p\) before letting \(n\to\infty\), and fix a bulk coordinate \(k\in\{2,\ldots,p\}\).  By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}fixed\mbox{-}dimensional\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}projection}\), the coordinate influences of the gradients at the origin are
\[
 \psi_{T,k}=\frac12SYq_k,\qquad
 \psi_{E,k}=\frac12S\left[\left(Y-\frac12\right)q_k-\mu_k\right],\qquad
 \psi_{D,k}=\frac12S\{Y-m(q)\}q_k,
\]
where \(\mu_k=0\), and that lemma gives
\[
 s_T:=\operatorname{Var}(\psi_{T,k})=\frac18,
 \qquad
 s_E:=\operatorname{Var}(\psi_{E,k})=\frac1{16},
 \qquad
 s_D:=\operatorname{Var}(\psi_{D,k})=\frac{v_\gamma}{4}.
\]
The same lemma also gives
\[
 \mathbb P(\mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n}\cap\mathcal Q_n)\longrightarrow1
\]
in the fixed-dimensional regime.  Thus the entropy-balanced influence and its variance refer to the unique exact-balancing weights on the certified event; no property of the uniform complement-event convention is being used.

For completeness, the curvature converting these score variances into the displayed regret coefficients follows directly from the empirical criterion.  Differentiating the defining identities gives
\[
 \sigma'(0)=\frac14,\qquad \sigma''(0)=0,
 \qquad h'(z)=z\sigma'(z),qquad h''(0)=\frac14.
\]
Consequently, for every \(j\in\mathcal J\), the sample Hessian at the origin is exactly
\[
 \nabla^2F_{jn}(0)
 =\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
 \{c_{j,ni}\sigma''(0)-\lambda h''(0)\}q_{ni}q_{ni}^{\top}
 =-\frac{\lambda}{4}\frac{Q_n^{\top}Q_n}{n}.
\]
By the Gaussian-feature assumption and the fixed-dimensional law of large numbers,
\[
 \frac{Q_n^{\top}Q_n}{n}\longrightarrow I_p
 \quad\text{almost surely},
\]
so the common limiting negative Hessian is \(\lambda I_p/4\).

Write \(G_{jn}=\nabla F_{jn}(0)\).  We now use precisely the proviso in the proposition: the certified-event remainder furnished by an affirmative joint system is uniform when the proportional limit is subsequently taken to \(\kappa\downarrow0\).  Applied to the global selector, that proviso makes the fixed-coordinate linearization uniform over the \(p_n-1\) bulk coordinates.  Thus it permits the two passages
\[
 \|G_{jn}\|_2^2=s_j\frac{p_n}{n}+o_{\mathbb P}(\kappa)
 =s_j\kappa+o_{\mathbb P}(\kappa)
\]
on the certified event and
\[
 \left\|\widehat\beta_{jn}-\frac4\lambda G_{jn}\right\|_2
 =o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt\kappa)
\]
after taking the proportional deterministic limit and then \(\kappa\downarrow0\).  Here the first equality aggregates the variance \(s_j/n\) of each bulk score coordinate, and the second uses the inverse of the common limiting negative Hessian \(\lambda I/4\).  The signal coordinate is only one coordinate, so its \(O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1})\) squared-score contribution vanishes in the proportional limit.  It follows that the deterministic norm selected by the joint system satisfies
\[
 \rho_j^2
 =\left(\frac4\lambda\right)^2s_j\kappa+o(\kappa)
 =\frac{16s_j}{\lambda^2}\kappa+o(\kappa),
 \qquad j\in\mathcal J.
\]
Since \(R>0\) is fixed, the last display also implies \(\rho_j<R\) for all sufficiently small positive \(\kappa\); thus the radius constraint is locally inactive in this reduction.

It remains to convert norm into regret.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}radial\mbox{-}invariance}\) gives
\[
 g'(r)=r\,\mathbb E\!\left[Z^2\sigma'(rZ)\right].
\]
Because \(0<\sigma'(x)\le 1/4\), dominated convergence, using \(\mathbb E Z^2=1\), yields
\[
 \lim_{r\downarrow0}\frac{g'(r)}r=\frac14.
\]
Since \(g(0)=0\), integration (equivalently, l'Hopital's rule) gives
\[
 g(r)=\frac{r^2}{8}+o(r^2)\qquad(r\downarrow0).
\]
The radial-regret identity in the same proposition and the preceding expansion therefore imply
\[
 r_j=\lambda g(\rho_j)
 =\frac{\lambda}{8}\rho_j^2+o(\kappa)
 =\frac{2s_j}{\lambda}\kappa+o(\kappa).
\]
Substitution of the three already established variances proves
\[
 r_T=\frac{\kappa}{4\lambda}+o(\kappa),\qquad
 r_E=\frac{\kappa}{8\lambda}+o(\kappa),\qquad
 r_D=\frac{v_\gamma\kappa}{2\lambda}+o(\kappa).
\]
All uses of the proportional-to-small-aspect-ratio interchange occur in the explicitly conditional aggregation step above; the fixed-dimensional variance and feasibility conclusions themselves require no such interchange.
